title: Destination-key scan must be shape-agnostic: walk all nested wrappers and count pair lists
answers: MemAlign base_judge destination kwargs not rejected
kwargs as list of pairs slips past validation
body:
Invariant: the destination-key check walks the entire serialized payload, not just the top-level third_party_scorer_data, because wrappers embed full scorers (ensemble_scorer_data.scorers, memory_augmented_judge_data.base_judge) that Scorer.model_validate rebuilds recursively.
Enforced by: mlflow/utils/validation.py:_iter_third_party_scorer_data yields every third_party_scorer_data mapping at any depth, and _find_destination_keys treats two-item [str, value] lists as keys because dict() accepts them.
What breaks if skipped: a sub-scorer with kwargs.api_base inside an ensemble or MemAlign judge is reconstructed and sent without rejection; a list-of-pairs kwargs bypasses a plain dict check.
Constraints: kwargs must be a JSON object or null (anything else is rejected with a clear message); do not assume a fixed nesting shape when adding wrapper types.
applies: Changes to the scorer payload validator or to any new scorer wrapper type that embeds serialized scorers.
says: Evaluation configs with nested judges can send requests to unapproved custom endpoints.
Ensemble scorers bypass endpoint validation when destination settings are nested inside sub-scorers.
Reject evaluation judge requests containing forbidden destination addresses inside nested configurations.
Validation fails to detect forbidden target URLs configured inside composite evaluators.
search: Destination-key validation must recursively traverse the entire serialized payload via mlflow/utils/validation.py:_iter_third_party_scorer_data to check embedded scorers such as ensemble_scorer_data.scorers and memory_augmented_judge_data.base_judge. In _find_destination_keys, two-item [str, value] lists are checked as keys because dict() accepts them, preventing list-of-pairs kwargs from bypassing checks. The kwargs payload must be a JSON object or null, and validation must not assume a fixed nesting shape.
